subject: math
title: Large Numbers and Decimals: Place Value to One Million and Thousandths
seo_title: Grade 6 Large Numbers and Decimals Worksheets: Place Value, Comparing and Rounding (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Read, represent, compare, and order whole numbers up to and including one million and decimal numbers up to thousandths, and round decimal numbers to the nearest tenth, hundredth, or whole number
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets for the Ontario curriculum: place value to one million, comparing and ordering large numbers, decimals to thousandths, and rounding to the nearest tenth, hundredth or whole number. 100 questions with an answer key, good EQAO practice.
key_big: Every place is worth 10 times the place to its right, from thousandths all the way up to one million.
key_sub: Compare decimals place by place, not by length: 0.5 = 0.50 > 0.45. To round, look one place to the right: 5 or more rounds up.
body_html:
Place value to one million

Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. Big numbers are split into groups of three digits: thousands and ones. In Canada we leave a small space between the groups (245 300), not a comma. A 4-digit number has no space (4536).

Words to digits

Write four hundred six thousand five in digits.

Four hundred six thousand → 406. Five → 005 (no hundreds and no tens, so write 0s).

Answer: 406 005

Ten hundred thousands make one million: 1 000 000.

Compare and order large numbers

First count the digits: a 6-digit number is greater than any 5-digit number. If both have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left until two digits are different.

Compare

571 020 ☐ 570 120

Hundred thousands: 5 = 5. Ten thousands: 7 = 7. Thousands: 1 > 0.

Answer: 571 020 > 570 120

Decimals to thousandths

After the decimal point come tenths, hundredths and thousandths. 1 hundredth split into 10 equal parts makes 10 thousandths. Read the word “and” as the decimal point.

Compare and order decimals

Compare the whole numbers first. Then give the decimals the same number of places by adding zeros at the end, and compare from the left: tenths, hundredths, thousandths.

Example

Order 0.5, 0.45 and 0.405 from least to greatest.

Write 0.500, 0.450 and 0.405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths.

Answer: 0.405, 0.45, 0.5

Rounding

  1. Find the place you are rounding to.
  2. Look at the digit one place to its right.
  3. 5 or more: round up. 4 or less: round down.
  4. Whole numbers: change the digits after that place to 0. Decimals: drop the digits after that place.
RoundLook atAnswer
749 607 to the nearest thousandthe hundreds digit: 6750 000
549 459 to the nearest hundred thousandthe ten thousands digit: 4500 000
4.68 to the nearest whole numberthe tenths digit: 65
4.68 to the nearest tenththe hundredths digit: 84.7
41.358 to the nearest hundredththe thousandths digit: 841.36
Watch the 9s

Round 12.95 to the nearest tenth.

The hundredths digit is 5, so round up. 9 tenths + 1 tenth = 10 tenths = 1 one. 12.9 becomes 13.0.

Answer: 13.0

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.45 > 0.5 because it has more digitsUse the same number of places: 0.45 < 0.50
Missing a zero (four hundred six thousand five → 46 005)Write each group as three digits: 406 | 005
Giving the digit, not its value (the 4 in 406 005 is 4)It is in the hundred thousands place: 400 000
Rounding the wrong place (4.68 to the nearest tenth → 5)Find the tenths digit first: 4.7
Cutting off instead of rounding (41.358 → 41.35)Look at the next digit: 8, so round up to 41.36
Rounding twice (549 459 → 550 000 → 600 000)Round the number you started with: 500 000

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about place value in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 6 (Number, B1) students read, represent, compare and order whole numbers up to one million and decimals to thousandths. They also round decimals to the nearest tenth, hundredth or whole number.

faq.q: Why do Canadian students write 245 300 with a space instead of a comma?
faq.a: Canada follows the SI style: numbers with 5 or more digits are split into groups of three with a small space, and 4-digit numbers have no space (4536). This avoids mix-ups with the decimal comma used in French.
0.5 is bigger. Write both with the same number of places, 0.45 and 0.50, and compare the tenths: 5 tenths is more than 4 tenths.

faq.q: How do you round a decimal to the nearest tenth?
faq.a: Look at the hundredths digit. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, keep the tenths digit. So 4.68 rounds to 4.7 and 4.63 rounds to 4.6.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 4 thousands = 4000. The digit is 4, but its value is 4000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 6 ten thousands = 60 000. The digit is 6, but its value is 60 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 3 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 3 hundreds = 300. The digit is 3, but its value is 300.

items.q: In 760 841, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 760 841 the ten thousands digit is 6, worth 60 000.

items.q: In 425 376, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 425 376 the thousands digit is 5, worth 5000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 4 hundred thousands = 400 000. The digit is 4, but its value is 400 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the tens place, so it is worth 6 tens = 60. The digit is 6, but its value is 60.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in 860 712?
items.e: The 6 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 6 ten thousands = 60 000. The digit is 6, but its value is 60 000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 5 in 589 471?
items.e: The 5 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 5 hundred thousands = 500 000. The digit is 5, but its value is 500 000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 1 in 851 794?
items.e: The 1 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 1 thousand = 1000. The digit is 1, but its value is 1000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 583 729?
items.e: The 7 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 7 hundreds = 700. The digit is 7, but its value is 700.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 300 000 + 40 000 + 700 + 2 = 340 702.

items.q: What number is 600 000 + 5000 + 30?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 600 000 + 5000 + 30 = 605 030.

items.q: Which number is four hundred six thousand five?
items.e: Write each group as three digits. Four hundred six thousand → 406. Then five → 005. Fill every empty place with 0: 406 005.

items.q: Which number is two hundred thirty thousand seven hundred eight?
items.e: Write each group as three digits. Two hundred thirty thousand → 230. Then seven hundred eight → 708. Fill every empty place with 0: 230 708.

items.q: Which number is nine hundred thousand four hundred thirty?
items.e: Write each group as three digits. Nine hundred thousand → 900. Then four hundred thirty → 430. Fill every empty place with 0: 900 430.

items.q: How do you write 305 070 in words?
c: three hundred thousand five hundred seventy
three hundred five thousand seven hundred
items.e: Split 305 070 into two groups: 305 thousand and 70. Say each group, then its name: three hundred five thousand seventy.

items.q: How do you write 140 602 in words?
c: one hundred four thousand six hundred two
one hundred forty thousand six hundred two
items.e: Split 140 602 into two groups: 140 thousand and 602. Say each group, then its name: one hundred forty thousand six hundred two.

items.q: How many thousands are there in one million?
items.e: 1 000 000 ÷ 1000 = 1000. Ten hundred thousands make one million, and each hundred thousand is 100 thousands: 10 × 100 = 1000 thousands.

items.q: In 550 000, the first 5 is worth how many times the second 5?
items.e: The first 5 is worth 500 000. The second 5 is worth 50 000. 500 000 ÷ 50 000 = 10. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. (450 000 is the difference, not how many times.)

sets.title: Compare and order numbers to one million

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 9 thousands is more than 8 thousands. So 609 845 > 608 945.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 102 300 has 6 digits and 98 765 has only 5, so 102 300 is greater. A big first digit does not matter when a number has fewer digits.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 1 thousand is more than 0 thousands. So 571 020 > 570 120.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 4 ten thousands is more than 0 ten thousands. So 340 560 > 304 560.

items.q: What is 10 000 more than 495 300?
items.e: Add 1 to the ten thousands digit: 9 ten thousands + 1 = 10 ten thousands. Regroup them as 1 hundred thousand: 4 + 1 = 5 hundred thousands. 495 300 + 10 000 = 505 300.

items.q: What is 10 000 less than 203 450?
items.e: There are 0 ten thousands, so regroup 1 hundred thousand as 10 ten thousands. 10 − 1 = 9 ten thousands and 1 hundred thousand is left. 203 450 − 10 000 = 193 450.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 9 ten thousands is more than 8 ten thousands. So 698 734 > 687 934. 698 734 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 9 ten thousands is more than 7 ten thousands. So 598 741 > 579 841. 598 741 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 99 875 has only 5 digits, so it is the least, even though it starts with 9. Of the 6-digit numbers: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 9 thousands is more than 8 thousands. So 109 800 > 108 900. 109 800 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 5 ten thousands is more than 4 ten thousands. So 951 486 > 948 516. 948 516 is the least.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 7 ten thousands is more than 3 ten thousands. So 573 649 > 537 946. 537 946 is the least.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 99 999 has only 5 digits, so it is the least. Every 6-digit number is at least 100 000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 300 000 to 400 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 10 000, not 1000. The arrow is 7 spaces after 300 000: 300 000 + 70 000 = 370 000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1 000 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 100 000. The arrow is 1 space after 500 000: 500 000 + 100 000 = 600 000.

items.q: Put 639 125, 619 235, 619 523 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 619 235 < 619 523 (hundreds: 2 < 5). 619 523 < 639 125 (ten thousands: 1 < 3). So the order is 619 235, 619 523, 639 125.

items.q: Put 475 183, 478 351, 473 581 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 473 581 < 475 183 (thousands: 3 < 5). 475 183 < 478 351 (thousands: 5 < 8). So the order is 473 581, 475 183, 478 351.

items.q: Put 623 784, 683 274, 628 374 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: Compare from the left. 623 784 < 628 374 (thousands: 3 < 8). 628 374 < 683 274 (ten thousands: 2 < 8). So the order is 683 274, 628 374, 623 784.

items.q: 52☐ 400 > 527 600. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred thousands and ten thousands are the same. Compare the thousands: the box must be 7 or more. If it is 7, compare the hundreds: 4 < 6, so 527 400 is too small. 528 400 > 527 600.

items.q: 3☐4 500 < 312 900. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred thousands are the same. Compare the ten thousands: the box must be 1 or less. If it is 1, compare the thousands: 4 > 2, so 314 500 is too big. 304 500 < 312 900.

items.q: Use each of the digits 4, 0, 8, 2, 6 and 9 once. What is the greatest 6-digit number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the hundred thousands place, then the next biggest, and so on: 9, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0. The greatest number is 986 420.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 4.307?
items.e: The red 7 is the third digit after the decimal point, in the thousandths place. Its value is 7 thousandths = 0.007. The 0 holds the hundredths place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 6.054?
items.e: The red 5 is the second digit after the decimal point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 5 hundredths = 0.05.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 13.582?
items.e: The red 5 is the first digit after the decimal point, in the tenths place. Its value is 5 tenths = 0.5.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 7.286?
items.e: 7 . 2 8 6: the 8 is the second digit after the decimal point, in the hundredths place. It is worth 8 hundredths = 0.08.

items.q: In which place is the digit 6 in 0.036?
items.e: 0 . 0 3 6: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. The 6 is in the thousandths place.

items.q: In 9.473, which digit is in the hundredths place?
items.e: After the decimal point the places are tenths (4), hundredths (7) and thousandths (3). So the hundredths digit is 7.

items.q: In 21.509, which digit is in the thousandths place?
items.e: After the decimal point: tenths 5, hundredths 0, thousandths 9. The thousandths digit is 9.

items.q: Which number is equal to 0.7?
items.e: A 0 at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 0.7 = 0.70 = 0.700. 0.07 and 0.007 have the 7 in a different place.

items.q: Write 5 ones, 4 hundredths and 1 thousandth as a decimal.
items.e: There are 0 tenths, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 5 . 0 4 1 = 5.041. 5.41 would have 4 tenths.
3 ones, 8 tenths, 2 hundredths and 7 thousandths: 3 . 8 2 7 = 3.827.

items.q: Which shows 6.135 in expanded form?
items.e: 6 ones, 1 tenth, 3 hundredths and 5 thousandths: 6 + 0.1 + 0.03 + 0.005.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 0.4?
items.e: 1 tenth = 100 thousandths, so 4 tenths = 400 thousandths. 0.4 = 0.400.

items.q: Write 0.045 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.045 has three decimal places, so it is thousandths: 45 thousandths = 451000. 45100 would be 0.45.

items.q: Which number is four and twenty-six thousandths?
items.e: “And” stands for the decimal point. Twenty-six thousandths must end in the third place after the point: 4.026. 4.26 would be twenty-six hundredths.

items.q: How do you read 0.305 in words?
items.e: 0.305 has three decimal places, so read the digits as a whole number and say “thousandths”: three hundred five thousandths.

items.q: In 3.33, the 3 in the tenths place is worth how many times the 3 in the hundredths place?
items.e: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. 0.3 = 10 × 0.03. So the answer is 10.

items.q: What number is 0.001 more than 5.309?
items.e: 9 thousandths + 1 thousandth = 10 thousandths = 1 hundredth. So 5.309 + 0.001 = 5.310 = 5.31. 5.319 adds 1 hundredth, not 1 thousandth.

items.q: What number is 0.01 more than 1.495?
items.e: Add 1 hundredth: 9 hundredths + 1 hundredth = 10 hundredths = 1 tenth. So 1.495 + 0.01 = 1.505. 1.496 adds only 1 thousandth.

items.q: What number is 0.1 less than 8.04?
items.e: Take away 1 tenth. 8.04 has 0 tenths, so regroup 1 one as 10 tenths: 8.04 − 0.1 = 7.94. 8.03 takes away 1 hundredth.

items.q: Use each of the digits 2, 7, 4 and 9 once to make the greatest number with 1 digit before the decimal point and 3 digits after it.
items.e: Put the largest digit in the ones place, then the next largest in the tenths, hundredths and thousandths places: 9.742. 2.479 is the least number you can make.

items.q: Compare 0.45 and 0.5.
items.e: 0.5 = 0.50. Compare the tenths: 4 tenths < 5 tenths. So 0.45 < 0.5. More digits does not mean a greater number.

items.q: Compare 0.6 and 0.58.
items.e: 0.6 = 0.60. Compare the tenths: 6 > 5. So 0.6 > 0.58.

items.q: Compare 3.08 and 3.080.
items.e: A 0 at the end does not change the value. 3.08 = 3.080, so 3.08 = 3.080.

items.q: Compare 0.007 and 0.07.
items.e: 0.07 = 0.070. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 7. So 0.007 < 0.07. 7 thousandths is less than 7 hundredths.

items.q: Compare 0.99 and 1.01.
items.e: Compare the ones first: 0 < 1. So 0.99 < 1.01. Any number less than 1 is less than any number greater than 1.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.600, 0.590, 0.599, 0.065. Compare the tenths first: only 0.6 has 6 tenths. So 0.6 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.304, 0.340, 0.400, 0.430. The least is 0.304, even though it has the most digits.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0.3 to 0.4 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth (0.01). Count 7 spaces on from 0.30: 0.37.

items.q: Compare 0.125 and 0.13.
items.e: Write both with 3 places: 0.125 and 0.130. The tenths are the same. Compare the hundredths: 2 < 3. So 0.125 < 0.13. Do not compare 125 with 13.

items.q: Compare 4.216 and 4.21.
items.e: 4.21 = 4.210. Ones, tenths and hundredths are the same. Compare the thousandths: 6 > 0. So 4.216 > 4.21.

items.q: Compare 2.8 and 2.799.
items.e: 2.8 = 2.800. The ones are the same. Compare the tenths: 8 > 7. So 2.8 > 2.799.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare the ones first: 6.998 has only 6 ones. Then 7.200, 7.190, 7.199: 2 tenths is more than 1 tenth. So 7.2 is the greatest.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 5.2 to 5.21 there are 10 equal spaces. 5.21 − 5.20 = 0.01, so each space is 1 thousandth. Count 4 spaces on from 5.200: 5.204.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 0.5, 0.45, 0.405
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.500, 0.450, 0.405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths. So 0.405, 0.45, 0.5.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 2.7, 2.07, 1.97, 2.069
items.e: 1.97 has only 1 one, so it is the least. Then write the rest with 3 places: 2.700, 2.070, 2.069. So 1.97, 2.069, 2.07, 2.7.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0.68 to 0.69 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 thousandth, not 1 hundredth. Count 3 spaces on from 0.680: 0.683.

items.q: Order from greatest to least: 5.3, 5.28, 5.305, 5.03
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 5.300, 5.280, 5.305, 5.030. Greatest first: 5.305, 5.3, 5.28, 5.03.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 0.8, 0.08, 0.808, 0.088
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.800, 0.080, 0.808, 0.088. Compare 800, 80, 808 and 88 thousandths. So 0.08, 0.088, 0.8, 0.808.

items.q: Which number is between 0.6 and 0.7?
items.e: 0.6 = 0.600 and 0.7 = 0.700. 0.608 is between them. 0.068 and 0.599 are less than 0.6, and 0.71 is more than 0.7.

items.q: 0.7☐7 < 0.74. What is the greatest digit that can go in the box?
items.e: 0.74 = 0.740. With 3 in the box: 0.737 < 0.740. With 4: 0.747 > 0.740. So the greatest digit is 3.

sets.title: Rounding decimals and large numbers in real life

items.q: A pumpkin at the fall fair has a mass of 4.68 kg. What is its mass to the nearest tenth of a kilogram?
items.e: 4.68 is between 4.6 and 4.7. Look at the hundredths digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up to 4.7. 4.6 kg just cuts off the 8. Answer: 4.7 kg.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Winnipeg had a population of 749 607. What is this rounded to the nearest thousand?
items.e: 749 607 is between 749 000 and 750 000. Look at the hundreds digit, one place to the right of the thousands: 6. 5 or more, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 thousands. Regroup them as 1 ten thousand. Answer: 750 000 people.

items.q: In gym class, Ethan ran 100 m in 14.37 seconds. What is his time to the nearest tenth of a second?
items.e: 14.37 is between 14.3 and 14.4. Look at the hundredths digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up to 14.4. Answer: 14.4 s.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Hamilton had a population of 569 353. What is this rounded to the nearest ten thousand?
items.e: 569 353 is between 560 000 and 570 000. Look at the thousands digit, one place to the right of the ten thousands: 9. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 570 000 people.

items.q: Owen walked 4.65 km in the Terry Fox Run. What is this distance to the nearest whole kilometre?
items.e: 4.65 is between 4 and 5. Look at the tenths digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up to 5. 4.7 km is the nearest tenth, not the nearest whole number. Answer: 5 km.

items.q: At the 2021 census, the city of Victoria had a population of 91 867. What is this rounded to the nearest ten thousand?
items.e: 91 867 is between 90 000 and 100 000. Look at the thousands digit, one place to the right of the ten thousands: 1. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 90 000 people.

items.q: A field trip to the science centre costs $18.65 per student. What is this to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $18.65 is between $18 and $19. Look at the tenths (dimes) digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up. $18.70 is the nearest ten cents, and $20 is the nearest ten dollars. Answer: $19.

items.q: A junior hockey team sold 148 652 tickets in one season. What is this rounded to the nearest thousand?
items.e: 148 652 is between 148 000 and 149 000. Look at the hundreds digit, one place to the right of the thousands: 6. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 149 000 tickets.

items.q: Gas costs $1.479 per litre. What is this price to the nearest cent (hundredth of a dollar)?
items.e: 1.479 is between 1.47 and 1.48. Look at the thousandths digit: 9. 5 or more, so round up to 1.48. A cent is a hundredth of a dollar, so keep two decimal places. Answer: $1.48.

items.q: Mei skated 500 m at the speed skating oval in 41.358 seconds. What is her time to the nearest hundredth of a second?
items.e: 41.358 is between 41.35 and 41.36. Look at the thousandths digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up to 41.36. 41.35 s just cuts off the 8, and 41.4 s rounds to the tenths. Answer: 41.36 s.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Québec City had a population of 549 459. What is this rounded to the nearest hundred thousand?
items.e: 549 459 is between 500 000 and 600 000. Look at the ten thousands digit, one place to the right of the hundred thousands: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Do not round twice (549 459 → 550 000 → 600 000). Answer: 500 000 people.

items.q: Priya jumped 3.475 m in the long jump at the track meet. What is this to the nearest hundredth of a metre?
items.e: 3.475 is exactly halfway between 3.47 and 3.48. A number that is exactly halfway rounds up. Answer: 3.48 m.

items.q: On a snow day, 12.95 cm of snow fell. What is this to the nearest tenth of a centimetre?
items.e: 12.95 is between 12.9 and 13.0. Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up. 9 tenths + 1 tenth = 10 tenths = 1 one, so 12.9 becomes 13.0. Do not write 12.10. Answer: 13.0 cm.

items.q: A bag of Ontario apples has a mass of 2.496 kg. What is this to the nearest hundredth of a kilogram?
items.e: 2.496 is between 2.49 and 2.50. Look at the thousandths digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up. 9 hundredths + 1 hundredth = 10 hundredths = 1 tenth, so 2.49 becomes 2.50. Answer: 2.50 kg.

items.q: Four swimmers raced 50 m. Which time does not round to 36.5 s to the nearest tenth?
items.e: Times from 36.45 s up to (but not including) 36.55 s round to 36.5 s. 36.44 has 4 hundredths, so it rounds down to 36.4 s.

items.q: A news report says that about 230 000 people lived in Windsor, Ontario, in 2021. The number was rounded to the nearest ten thousand. Which could be the real population?
items.e: Numbers from 225 000 to 234 999 round to 230 000. 229 660 is in that range. 235 000 and 239 000 round up to 240 000, and 224 800 rounds down to 220 000.

items.q: Hana’s 400 m time, rounded to the nearest tenth, is 52.3 seconds. Which could be her real time?
items.e: Times from 52.25 s to 52.34 s round to 52.3 s. 52.26 s is in that range. 52.36 s and 52.35 s round up to 52.4 s, and 52.21 s rounds down to 52.2 s.

items.q: The population of a town, rounded to the nearest ten thousand, is 250 000. What is the least the population could be?
items.e: Numbers from 245 000 to 254 999 round to 250 000. 244 999 would round down to 240 000, so the least is 245 000. (254 999 is the greatest.)

items.q: A race time rounded to the nearest tenth is 12.7 s. The real time was measured to the hundredth. What is the least it could be?
items.e: Times from 12.65 s to 12.74 s round to 12.7 s. 12.64 s would round down to 12.6 s, so the least is 12.65 s. (12.74 s is the greatest.)

items.q: Kai’s ski race time was 48.346 s. He rounded it to the nearest hundredth (48.35 s), then rounded that to the nearest tenth and got 48.4 s. What is 48.346 s rounded to the nearest tenth?
items.e: Always round the number you started with. 48.346 is between 48.3 and 48.4. Look at the hundredths digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down to 48.3 s. Rounding twice gives the wrong answer.
